overview: This event ties together crosswind takeoff and approach and landing, ocf, and contact unusual attitudes in a way that should already make sense before you step. You should be ready to brief what changes the plan, what numbers matter, and where the usual errors start once the workload climbs.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: use crab and wing-low techniques to stay aligned with the runway in crosswind conditions. Adjust bank, power, and control inputs as needed; waveoff if overbanking is required

children.text: Know the entry airspeed, altitude, configuration, and cockpit setup before you start the maneuver.
Failure to reduce aileron as speed builds.
Improper rudder use leading to drift or weathervaning.
Skipping due to premature liftoff on upwind wing.
Max AOB 45°; waveoff if more is required
+½ gust factor to final approach speed (max +10 kts)
Use rudder/brakes to stay straight; brakes below 80 KIAS

items.text: Improper/aggressive controls near stall, mechanical failure, atmospheric conditions, or combinations.

children.text: Aircraft moves unpredictably after stall; controls may feel ineffective or reversed.
Uncommanded rapid motions, controls ineffective; neutral controls + idle power recommended.

items.text: recovery from NH, NL, or Inverted attitudes due to disorientation, misflown maneuvers, or external factors. Recovery is visual (VFR) and must be completed above 6000’ AGL

children.text: Use back stick to bring nose to horizon
Roll upright as nose approaches horizon
Roll wings level, raise nose, check oil pressure, power as req.

studyNotes.summary: Have Crosswind Takeoff and Approach and Landing, plus OCF organized before step so the cockpit workload never outruns the brief.
